spec.flattening: row-major (C-order) flatten of each (N, N) matrix; the top level of 'scores' is a list over datasets
spec.lags: optional, same shape; positive int lag, 0 for instantaneous. Only read where the link is predicted present.
metrics: AUC (ROC) over all N*N entries EXCLUDING SELF-LINKS, pooled over the B datasets of an experiment
FPR / TPR from the p-values at alpha=0.05
F-measure with beta=0.5 (precision-weighted) from the p-values
TLR (true lag rate) among correctly predicted links
spec.note: This harness NEVER uploads. causeme_build_submission writes a local file only.
spec.orientation: A_ij is the score for the link i -> j (CAUSE row, EFFECT column) -- the TRANSPOSE of this repo's convention, so a BaselineResult must be transposed before submission (see causeme_matrix_from_result).
spec.pvalues: optional, same shape; thresholded at 5% for the binary metrics
spec.reference_baseline: the shipped example method is a statsmodels VAR (trend='nc') on z-scored data that stores, per ordered pair, |coef| at the lag with the smallest p-value, with p-values Bonferroni-multiplied by maxlags
spec.scores: non-negative reals, higher = more confident; 0 = certain absence
what_an_entry_requires: 1. Register the METHOD on causeme.uv.es (name, parameters, description, optional paper/code URL). Uploading a code zip whose module exposes `my_method(data, **params) -> (val_matrix, p_matrix, lag_matrix)` is what lets CauseMe mark a result 'Validated'.
2. Registration returns a `method_sha` that identifies the method.
3. Download an experiment zip from Data and Models. It contains a few hundred .txt datasets, each loadable with np.loadtxt -> (T, N). Results MUST be ordered by sorted(filename).
4. Run the method on every dataset, collect the matrices, and write ONE bz2-compressed JSON dict.
5. Upload that .json.bz2 on 'My Results'. Uploads per user are rate limited.
